reason: E2 shows annealing induces nanoscale clusters, supporting the first premise. E1 states that disorder broadens the specific heat jump, supporting the last premise. However, no cited evidence supports the core mechanistic premises that such ordering reduces electronic scattering or enhances Tc; E3 discusses disorder suppressing or enhancing Tc in different contexts but does not link partial ordering to reduced scattering or a sharper transition.
premises: Thermal annealing of the HEA induces nanoscale short-range ordering (clustering) without secondary phases.
Nanoscale ordering reduces electronic scattering from compositional disorder.
Reduced scattering enhances the effective Cooper pairing interaction (BCS mechanism).
Enhanced pairing yields a more homogeneous superconducting state with higher Tc and sharper transition.
In disordered superconductors, inhomogeneity broadens the specific heat jump at Tc.
